paper_admission: NeurIPS 2025 primary PDF explicitly links official repository on page 1

observations.extra_optimization: MINGLE.test_time_adaptation constructs torch.optim.Adam, calls loss.backward(), optional project_gradient(), then optimizer.step(); gate weight and bias are trainable
observations.subspace: LoRAMoE inputs are flattened across examples/tokens; raw sum X.T@X is decomposed without centering; truncated bases are concatenated and QR-orthonormalized
observations.soft_projection: project_gradient returns G - (G @ U * lambda) @ U.T, i.e. G(I-U Lambda U.T); not G U Lambda U.T as displayed in primary paper Eq10 combined with Eq11
observations.bias: project_gradient returns rank-1 bias gradients unchanged because grad.dim()!=2
observations.initialization: Gate weights are normal(std=0.01), bias is init_lambda=0 at creation; not zero-initialized weight as paper Algorithm1
observations.forward: gate(hidden_states) is token-averaged, optionally batch-averaged; scalar per-expert gates form an input-dependent weight W0 + sum g_j(X) T_j
observations.test_data: test_time_adaptation uses the current task test dataset and select_seed_subset stratifies by labels; adaptation batches discard labels. This is not our train-calibration protocol
observations.no_parameter_reprojection: Reviewed adaptation loop projects gradients before Adam; no post-step constraint projection appears in that loop
observations.limitation: Static source review of three pinned files, not an execution, empirical criticism, complete dependency audit or model-merging defense reproduction

analytic_counterexample.kind: Own deterministic algebra illustration, not MINGLE execution or a CLIP experiment
analytic_counterexample.claim: A projected gradient can yield a non-null Adam parameter update; zero initialization, unchanged bias and features alone do not fix this. It does not refute the paper empirical results.
